title: A band of brothers, not a gallery of stars
news: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino, spotted at 13 by Marcelo Bielsa and mentored by Sir Alex Ferguson, built his best teams on 'respect and love', trust and camaraderie.
syllabus: Leadership; emotional intelligence; mentorship and work culture
link: Pochettino's teams succeeded where he built trust and team spirit, and struggled where there was 'too much greatness' and too many egos. Leadership rooted in respect, mentorship and patience gets more from the same people than leadership by command, a lesson for heads of public offices.
question: "Teams are built on trust, not authority." How can a civil servant use emotional intelligence and mentorship to transform the work culture of an office?

src: IE p. 13 (Idea Exchange: Sjoerd Marijne & Savita Punia)
title: A team that owns its vision
news: After two poor years, the women's hockey team asked for coach Sjoerd Marijne's return; he rebuilt cohesion through shared ownership, and the team won Asian Games gold and an Olympic berth.
syllabus: Leadership; Team building and motivation; Emotional intelligence; Work culture
link: Leadership that shares the vision, invites players to speak up and lets them meet without the coach builds ownership; authority grows when it is shared.
question: "A leader's vision succeeds only when the team owns it." Discuss with examples from public service.
